The remaining issues mean:

1. **Software differences**

The **96 verified files** mean the download is intact. The passing tests check particular pieces; the remaining failures identify work needed before everything runs together.

**Our next step is to show BeamNG’s camera picture inside the Sunnypilot UI, then add vehicle data and simulator steering.**

records.topic: What Sunnypilot needs from the BeamNG PC
records.owner_message: see i have connected the pc with beamng ,lets work on this ,now pc beamng will act as a real car ,wat are the things we need by sunnypilot to make it work

original_final_answers.text:
**Yes—BeamNG can provide the simulated car while Sunnypilot runs on Radxa.** For your selected setup, the loop is:

**BeamNG → monitor → Radxa webcam → Sunnypilot → Chimera → CAN → PC → BeamNG**

Sunnypilot needs these parts:

| Needed | What we must supply |
|---|---|
| **Road view** | Webcam aimed at the game’s forward view. Our camera/model path has prior bench validation; screen alignment and delay still need checking. |
| **Vehicle state** | Speed, four wheel speeds, measured steering angle, pedals, gear, ignition, cruise buttons and override/fault status. |
| **Motion sensors** | Simulated acceleration and rotation from BeamNG. Radxa’s stationary physical IMU cannot describe the moving game car. |
| **Car parameters** | The selected BeamNG car’s wheelbase, mass, steering ratio, steering limits and response delay. |
| **CAN interface** | PC Waveshare gateway, agreed message definitions, and a Chimera backend compatible with Sunnypilot. These remain to be implemented. |
| **Returning controls** | Translate Sunnypilot’s final steering, throttle and brake commands into game inputs, including engage/cancel and timeout behavior. |

BeamNG supports custom Lua telemetry protocols, giving us a documented route to extract vehicle data. Its basic OutGauge telemetry alone is incomplete for this loop. [Official documentation](https://docs.beamng.com/modding/protocols/)

**Our first working milestone should be receive-only:** watch the game through the webcam and display truthful BeamNG speed, steering and motion in Sunnypilot. Then log controller outputs, followed by game-only control.

I confirmed Radxa’s Ethernet link is up and `10.43.0.216` appears reachable. SSH stopped at missing trusted host-key verification, so the current game, car and mods remain unverified.

I saved the checklist in the [BeamNG guide](/home/radxa/comma/sunnypilot/openpilot/tools/sim/beamng/README.md:28), committed as `dd29f00`. Documentation checks pass; the live loop is still pending.

records.topic: All data our DBC can get
records.owner_message: I WANT U TO tell wat all data our dbc can get

original_final_answers.text:
Our **[ocelot_controls.dbc](/home/radxa/comma/sunnypilot/opendbc_repo/opendbc/dbc/ocelot_controls.dbc:38)** defines **20 CAN message types containing 120 fields**. Those fields include readings, commands and message checks—not 120 separate sensors.

It can describe these incoming readings **when the hardware or BeamNG adapter sends matching messages**:

| Source | Data available in the DBC |
|---|---|
| **Steering-angle sensor** | Steering-wheel angle, turning-speed magnitude, sensor state |
| **Engine / ignition** | Engine RPM, ignition on/off, brake pressed, crank-sensor pulse timing and count |
| **Vehicle-speed sensor** | Vehicle-speed value, speed-sensor pulse timing and count |
| **Cruise buttons** | On/off, cancel, set/down, resume/up, two raw analog-input readings |
| **Accelerator interceptor** | Two accelerator-pedal sensor channels and module state |
| **Accelerator actuator** | Throttle position, speed-sensor and encoder readings, module state |
| **Steering interceptor** | Two steering sensor channels, driver-override indication, module state |
| **Steering actuator** | Driver torque, motor/EPS torque, healthy/fault status |
| **Brake actuator** | Pedal position, driver pressing brake, brake applied, healthy/fault and extended status |
| **Legacy SSC steering module** | Steering angle, speed, torque, module temperature, control/debug states |
| **Legacy iBooster** | Brake position, brake-applied indications and health/fault status |
| **Legacy relay module** | Relay status and state—retained in the file, but excluded from your build |

Messages also contain **checksums and sequence counters**; several include operating modes.

The DBC separately defines **outgoing accelerator, steering and brake commands**, plus legacy relay commands. Our live RetroPilot interface remains receive-only.

**It does not define** gear selection, individual wheel speeds, seatbelt/door status, indicators, fuel/battery level, GPS, IMU measurements or radar tracks.

**Not every defined reading is already used by Sunnypilot.** Speed scaling still needs confirmation, and pedal/interceptor channels need calibration before we can reliably call them percentages or physical torque.

It lacks gear, individual wheel speeds, GPS/IMU, radar and several factory statuses.

records.topic: Does it include dzid stepper control and ZSS angle?
records.owner_message: does it have dzid dbc to contronl stepper motor ,then Zss  steering angle

original_final_answers.text:
**Yes—our DBC already contains definitions for both.**

| Purpose | Message | CAN ID |
|---|---|---|
| Send angle/torque requests to the **dzid stepper controller** | `STEERING_COMMAND_SSC` | `0x22E` |
| Receive dzid motor position, speed, torque and status | `STEERING_STATUS_SSC` | `0x22F` |
| Receive **ZSS steering-wheel angle** and turning-speed magnitude | `STEER_ANGLE_SENSOR` | `0x50` |

The **dzid board drives the motor**, while **ZSS measures the steering angle**. The DBC carries motor requests; dzid firmware handles the motor drive.

Two details matter:

- **dzid:** The firmware we reviewed uses a different checksum from ours. Checksum handling, controller integration and calibration still need adaptation; live dzid control is not enabled.
- **ZSS:** Our updated **ZSS v0.2 code already matches `0x50`**, including its checksum. Physical calibration/testing remains pending. The original smartZSS `0x23` format is different.

These definitions are already in [our DBC](/home/radxa/comma/sunnypilot/opendbc_repo/opendbc/dbc/ocelot_controls.dbc:139).

records.topic: Are these analog inputs converted to CAN?
records.owner_message: so this bascially anglog inputs right which converted to can t

original_final_answers.text:
**Yes—for analog sensors, that is the idea:**

**Sensor voltage → Chimera/Interceptor reads it → CAN message → Sunnypilot**

For example, this applies to accelerator-pedal and steering torque-sensor signals.

Some inputs are digital: **our ZSS reads an encoder and sends the calculated steering angle over CAN.**

Motor control goes the other direction:

**Sunnypilot request → CAN → dzid/Actuator controller → motor**

The **firmware performs these conversions**. The **DBC describes how the values are packed into CAN messages**.

records.answer_summary: For analog sensors, MCU firmware reads voltage and packs CAN values. ZSS instead reads a digital encoder. Commands travel the reverse direction through the actuator controller. Firmware performs conversions; the DBC describes encoding.

records.topic: Can Sunnypilot read OEM CAN using a second DBC?
records.owner_message: wat if i connect to cars can bus to get data ,can sunnypilot can take input from 2 dbc files

original_final_answers.text:
**Yes. Sunnypilot can use two or more DBC files simultaneously.**

For our project:

| DBC | What it would read |
|---|---|
| **Your car’s original DBC** | Available factory data: speed, RPM, brake switch, gear, buttons, etc. |
| **Our RetroPilot DBC** | ZSS steering angle, interceptor readings and actuator feedback |

Each DBC gets its own message reader. Our `CarState` code then combines the readings into the vehicle information Sunnypilot uses.

**Our current RetroPilot port only has the RetroPilot reader.** We would need to add the correct car-specific reader and decide which source supplies each value.

Both readers can use one CAN bus when message IDs do not conflict. If the car and retrofit modules use the same IDs for different messages, they need separate CAN channels or an explicit translation.

records.answer_summary: Yes: independent DBC parsers can feed one combined CarState. An OEM DBC could supply available factory data while RetroPilot supplies retrofit feedback. Our current port only has its RetroPilot parser; OEM mapping, health, units/source priority and ID conflicts still need explicit implementation.
records.status_at_backfill: Supported architecture, not already-added OEM support. Separate channels or translation may be necessary for conflicting IDs.
